Resting-EEG baseline for rTMS remission (TDBRAIN) — pilot report

Bottom line: in this pilot, conventional resting EEG features (spectral power, frontal alpha asymmetry, entropy, wPLI connectivity) did not predict remission or response better than chance (cross-validated AUC about 0.4–0.54; label-permutation p = 0.24 for E01 seed 42). Adding FAA/entropy/connectivity to the spectral panel did not make E01 better than chance (AUC 0.49–0.54); against the spectral-only panel it was not consistently better (see numeric check in the figure captions; one repeat, seed 44, shows a gain because E01-PSD itself scored below chance there). This is a negative baseline result in 164 patients, not evidence for or against the proposed oddball idea.

Question and status

The original question (does task-vs-rest EEG reconfiguration add predictive information?) cannot be tested: the downloaded rTMS patients have eyes-open and eyes-closed resting EEG only; no oddball EEG exists for them (all 162 local oddball files belong to 129 healthy participants). Experiments E02–E05 are blocked_missing_rTMS_oddball and untested. This report covers only the conventional resting baseline: E00 (no information: training prevalence), E01-PSD (53 spectral features: band power in 3 regions for EC/EO, individual alpha frequency, EC/EO alpha contrast) and E01 (65 features: adds FAA, spectral entropy, 8 EO theta/alpha connectivity summaries). Prediction target: Remitter (primary), Responder (secondary). These are established controls, not a novel contribution.

Cohort

164 independent patients (session 1, assuming it precedes treatment per dataset convention — not individually verified; no dates available), 78 remitters (48%), 97 responders (59%). 3 people with only a session-2 workbook row were excluded. All recordings: ~120 s at 500 Hz, 26 scalp EEG channels. Features were computed once, outcome-blind; models used 5-fold patient-level cross-validation (3 repeats), one regularized logistic regression, thresholds from training data only.

Limitations

  • Small cohort (164): AUC intervals are wide (about ±0.1); a modest true effect could be missed.
  • Session-1-as-baseline is a convention, not verified timing.
  • 26 scalp channels, linked-mastoid reference, ~2 min per condition; connectivity uses only 20 four-second epochs (9 patients lacked enough clean epochs and were imputed).
  • Bipolar EOG pairing (VPVA−VNVB, HPHL−HNHR) is an assumption from channel names. Only EC/EO and no gamma.
  • Bootstrap intervals are conditional on saved out-of-fold predictions; CV repeats share the same patients.
  • E00 pooled AUC (0.49) is below 0.5 purely from fold-to-fold prevalence variation.
  • Connectivity matrices were not saved and no heatmaps were produced; IAF/entropy reliability not shown.
  • The 104 + 60 replication recordings were not used (blinded, headers only).

Next decision

Stop the conventional-baseline direction here. The oddball hypothesis remains untested; the next step is to ask whether matched pretreatment rTMS oddball data exist (the dataset authors historically described oddball data as available on request; not confirmed for these patients, and no one has been contacted). A new EC/EO feature would need its own hypothesis and a protocol amendment.
